description: Use for 'why does X work this way', 'why we picked Y', design rationale, regressions, postmortems, or data-backed thresholds. Returns a cited read on decisions and tradeoffs. Use how for runtime behavior.

compare.without: Guesses a reason from the code itself.
compare.with: Reads the commits and PR discussions behind it and each later change, then other sources if the trail is thin.

compare.without: States a guessed reason as if it were fact.
compare.with: Quotes what the authors wrote and marks its own inferences as inferences.

compare.without: Pieces together an answer even when the record has none.
compare.with: Says what the record does not answer.

brief.intro: It answers why from the record, not the code: the commits and PR discussions, then other sources if the trail is thin. It cites the authors, marks inferences, and names what the record leaves open.

lessons.quote: Answer from the record, not the code: read the commits and PR discussions that introduced the target and each later change, and other sources if the trail is thin.
lessons.quoteTr: Answer from the record, not the code: read the commits and PR discussions that introduced the target and each later change, and other sources if the trail is thin.
lessons.title: Name where the answer lives
lessons.does: It reads the original commits and PR discussions instead of inventing a plausible reason from the code.
lessons.why: Code shows what, not why; naming which record to read, through every later change, leaves no room to hand in a guess.
lessons.try: When you ask why, point to the source: "Read the commit and discussion that added this setting, and each change since, not just today's code."

lessons.quote: Cite what the authors wrote, mark your own inferences as inferences, and say what the record does not answer.
lessons.quoteTr: Cite what the authors wrote, mark your own inferences as inferences, and say what the record does not answer.
lessons.title: Ask for facts and guesses apart
lessons.does: Quotes from the authors, its own inferences and the open gaps come apart, so you know which lines to trust outright.
lessons.why: A "why" story is easy to smooth over; labeling inferences and naming the gaps keeps guesses out of the facts.
lessons.try: When you ask why, add: "Quote what has a source, mark your own guesses 'guess', and say plainly what you couldn't find."

lessons.title: Say what isn't its job
lessons.does: Questions about runtime behavior go to `how`, instead of being answered from history.
lessons.why: "When to use" alone lets neighboring tools step on each other; adding who handles the rest draws the line.
lessons.try: When you split up work, mark the edge: "You handle the copy; layout questions go to design, don't change it yourself."
